settings.uiScaleHint: Text and controls of the whole app. Terminals keep their own font size (Terminal settings).

hosts.startupHint: One command per line, typed after login. Script steps: expect <regex>, wait <seconds>, timeout <seconds>, sendSecret <vault scope>, send <text>.
hosts.jumpHint: The connection goes through these hosts in order. Each hop uses its own user, key and password.
hosts.proxyCommandHint: %h, %p and %r are replaced with host, port and user. Presets cover AWS SSM, GCP IAP, Cloudflare and Teleport.
hosts.passwordCommandHint: Prints the password on standard output (password manager, Vault…). $SHELLVANE_HOST, $SHELLVANE_PORT and $SHELLVANE_USER describe the target.
hosts.certificateCommandHint: Signs the key in $SHELLVANE_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE and prints a short-lived OpenSSH certificate, requested at every connection.
hosts.forwardAgentHint: The server can use your agent's keys; Shellvane asks before every signature.

totp.label: Two-factor code (TOTP)
totp.hint: Codes are generated automatically when the server asks for them. The secret is stored in the vault.
totp.needsVault: Unlock the vault to store a TOTP secret.

hosts.multiplexerHint: Runs the shell inside tmux or screen on the server: after a disconnection, reconnecting brings back the same programs and output. Falls back to the plain shell when not installed.
hosts.kubeHint: Each pane on this host gets its own kubectl context on the server (kubectl, helm and k9s follow it); the shared kubeconfig is never changed. Empty inherits.
hosts.connectAll: Connect to all hosts in a grid
hosts.environmentHint: NAME=value, one per line; exported before the shell starts.
hosts.remoteCommandHint: Runs instead of the interactive shell; the pane ends when it exits.

status.unknown: Reached through a jump host or proxy

hosts.showStatusHint: Checks the SSH port of directly reachable hosts every minute while the hosts panel is open.
hosts.forwardX11Hint: Graphical programs started on the server (xclock, gitk, virt-manager) open on this computer. Needs a local X server: XQuartz on macOS, VcXsrv or X410 on Windows.
hosts.authCustom: Choose the authentication methods and their order
hosts.authOrderHint: Unchecked methods are never used. Every key is tried in turn, the host's key first, then the agent's and those in ~/.ssh.
hosts.identitiesOnlyHint: For servers that refuse after a few keys (MaxAuthTries): offer only the key chosen above.

template.copied: Groups of {{name}} copied, without hosts: paste them in Shellvane on another computer.
template.intro: Paste a group exported from Shellvane: its subgroups, settings and hosts, if they were included. It never holds keys or secrets.
template.mergeHint: Groups that already exist with the same name are kept as they are and receive what they lack; hosts already present with the same name and address are skipped.
template.imported: {created, plural, =0 {No new groups} one {1 group created} other {# groups created}}, {reused, plural, =0 {none already present} one {1 already present} other {# already present}}; {hosts, plural, =0 {no new hosts} one {1 host added} other {# hosts added}}{skipped, plural, =0 {} one {, 1 already present} other {, # already present}}.
template.exportIntro: Copies the group, its subgroups and their settings to the clipboard, to paste in Shellvane on another computer. Vault keys, passwords, notes, local themes, Wake-on-LAN addresses and knock sequences are never included.
template.withHosts: Include the hosts (name, address, tags, settings and jump hosts)
template.copiedWithHosts: {{name}} copied with its hosts: paste it in Shellvane on another computer.
template.commandsLeftOut: For safety, these commands were not imported (add them by hand if you trust them): {{commands}}

hosts.preConnectCommandHint: Runs on this computer before every connection, with $SHELLVANE_HOST, $SHELLVANE_USER and the host's public key in $SHELLVANE_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE (when an SSH key is chosen); connecting stops if it fails. EC2 Instance Connect pushes the key for 60 seconds: the host name must be the instance ID, usually with the AWS SSM proxy command.

picker.search: Search by name, address, group or tag

hosts.credentialPlugin: Credentials from a plugin or a team
hosts.credentialPluginMissing: A plugin configuration that no longer exists
hosts.credentialPluginHint: HashiCorp Vault, CyberArk, Conjur, Teleport or Boundary give the login at every connection (a short-lived certificate, a password, the broker’s user and proxy). Set them up in Plugins.

hint.awsSsm: Needs the aws CLI and the Session Manager plugin, logged in (aws sso login). The instance needs no public address or open port.
hint.azureBastion: Needs the Azure CLI with the ssh and bastion extensions, logged in (az login), and a Standard Bastion with native client support. Shellvane opens a tunnel on a free local port.
hint.gcpIap: Needs the gcloud CLI, logged in (gcloud auth login), and a firewall rule allowing IAP to port 22.

kerberos.label: Kerberos / Active Directory (GSSAPI)
kerberos.hint: Single sign-on with the domain: the ticket of your computer's login or kinit is used; without one, Shellvane asks the domain password and gets a ticket. Realm and principal are needed only when the user name and the host's domain do not tell them.

vault.title: Vault
vault.intro: The vault keeps passwords and key passphrases encrypted on this computer. Create a master password to start.
vault.noRecovery: If you forget the master password, saved secrets can only be recovered with a recovery key: create one after setting up the vault.
vault.isUnlocked: The vault is unlocked. It locks itself after 15 minutes of inactivity.

enable.touchid: Use Touch ID to unlock from now on
enable.hello: Use Windows Hello to unlock from now on

gate.title: Unlock the vault
gate.intro: This needs a secret from the vault. Enter the master password to continue.

vault.none: No saved credentials. Tick “Save in vault” when you log in.
vault.unavailable: The vault is available in the desktop app.
vault.forgot: Forgot the password? Use the recovery key
vault.recovered: Vault unlocked with the new password.
vault.recoveryNotSet: No recovery key: if you forget the password, saved secrets are lost.
vault.recoveryShowOnce: Write this key down and keep it somewhere safe, away from this computer. It is shown only now; with it anyone can set a new master password.
vault.keychainHint: The vault opens at startup without the master password, with a secret kept in the macOS Keychain, the Windows Credential Manager or GNOME Keyring/KWallet. Anyone who can use your session on this computer can open it; the master password keeps working.

import.title: Import

hints.openssh: Reads Host blocks and the files they include. LocalForward, RemoteForward and DynamicForward become tunnels.
hints.putty: Reads saved SSH sessions and their port forwardings. Passwords are not stored by PuTTY.
hints.kitty: Reads saved SSH sessions with their folders. For portable KiTTY choose the Sessions folder next to kitty.exe. The folder can also be given as a .zip; its subfolders become groups.
hints.mobaxterm: Reads SSH sessions and folders of MobaXterm.ini or a .mxtsessions export.
hints.securecrt: Reads the Sessions folder; subfolders become groups.
hints.winscp: Reads SFTP and SCP sites of WinSCP.ini. If WinSCP stores its settings in the registry, export them first (Tools → Export configuration).
hints.filezilla: Reads the SFTP sites of sitemanager.xml, with their folders.
hints.tabby: Reads SSH profiles of config.yaml, with groups and jump hosts.
hints.mremoteng: Reads SSH connections of confCons.xml, with their folders.
hints.termius: In Termius export the hosts as an SSH config file, then choose it here.

keys.rotateHint: Rotation creates a new key of the same type, installs it on these hosts, logs in with it alone to check it works, then makes the hosts and groups use it. If a host fails, nothing is switched.
keys.removeOld: Then remove the old key from the hosts' authorized_keys
keys.rotated: Hosts and groups now use {{name}}. The old key is still in Shellvane: delete it when you no longer need it.
keys.notSwitched: {{name}} was created but not every host accepted it: hosts and groups still use the old key.
keys.exportHint: The private key of {{name}} in the chosen format. With a passphrase it is encrypted; without, anyone with the text can use it.
keys.exported: Private key of {{name}} copied to the clipboard.
keys.deleteUsed: {name} is used by {count, plural, one {1 host} other {# hosts}}, which will no longer log in with it. Delete it?
keys.agentHint: Offers the vault's keys to other programs (ssh, git, scp) through SSH_AUTH_SOCK, asking before each signature. Keys are offered only while the vault is unlocked.
keys.agentCopy: Copy the line that sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK

token.add: Add a key from a hardware token
token.title: Key on a hardware token
token.intro: Use a key kept on a YubiKey, a smart card or an HSM: its private part never leaves the device, which signs after its PIN. Shellvane talks to it through the PKCS#11 module of its maker (OpenSC, Yubico's ykcs11…).
token.moduleFound: Modules found on this computer are listed; another library can be typed in.
token.moduleHint: No module found in the usual places: install OpenSC (or Yubico's PIV tool) and type the path of its PKCS#11 library.
token.none: No token found: plug it in and try again.
token.noKeys: This token has no keys with a public key or certificate Shellvane can read.
token.added: Key {{name}} added: assign it to hosts with SSH key.
token.noRotation: A key on a hardware token cannot be rotated from here: create a new key on the token, add it, then assign it.

automation.auditHint: Every automatic response is recorded here (never the secrets). Export it as CSV or JSON.

updates.title: Updates
updates.auto: Check for updates at startup and every few hours

blocked.readOnly: Shellvane cannot write to its own folder. Install the update from the release page, or move Shellvane to a folder you can write to.

updates.noRelease: No release has been published yet: there is nothing to update to.
updates.support: Shellvane is free, with every feature. If it saves you time, you can support it.

prompt.readyText: Restart Shellvane to use it, now or later: otherwise it starts the next time you open the app.

sync.title: Sync
sync.intro: Keep hosts, groups, snippets, tunnels, rules, environments, runbooks and color schemes in step between your computers through a folder they share (Syncthing, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, OneDrive, a network share), a WebDAV server, a Git repository or an S3 bucket. Everything is encrypted with a passphrase before it leaves this computer.
sync.needVault: Unlock the vault to set up sync: the folder key is kept there.
sync.passphraseHint: Use the same passphrase on every computer. It is not your master password and cannot be recovered.
sync.lockedHint: The vault is locked: sync waits until it is unlocked.
sync.noDevices: No other computer has synced to this folder yet.
sync.kind: Where to keep the encrypted files
sync.webdavHint: Nextcloud, ownCloud, a NAS or any WebDAV server: Shellvane creates the folder if it is missing. The password is kept in the vault; an app password is best.
sync.gitHint: A private repository you can already push to with git (SSH key or credential helper). Each computer commits only its own encrypted file; the repository sees nothing in clear.
sync.s3Hint: Amazon S3 or a compatible service (MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi). Files go in the bucket's Shellvane-sync folder; the secret key is kept in the vault. A key limited to that bucket is best.

welcome.title: Welcome to Shellvane
welcome.intro: Shellvane keeps your SSH hosts, keys and tunnels in one place. This short tour sets up the vault and brings in the hosts you already have; every step can be done later from the guide.

vault.title: Create the vault
vault.intro: The vault keeps passwords, key passphrases and two-factor seeds, encrypted with a master password that never leaves this computer.
vault.hint: Choose a long password you can remember: it cannot be recovered, but you can create a recovery key in Settings → Vault.
vault.ready: The vault is already set up.

import.title: Bring in your hosts
import.intro: Import hosts from OpenSSH, PuTTY, MobaXterm, SecureCRT, Termius and other tools, or add one by hand.
import.none: No other tool was found in its usual place; you can still choose a file in the import dialog.

done.title: You are ready
done.palette: {{keys}} searches hosts, snippets, actions and this guide.
done.quick: Quick connect at the top accepts user@host, telnet:// and serial:// addresses.
done.guide: The guide's Getting started page tracks what is left to set up.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.intro: Install only the plugins you need. Inventories bring in hosts from clouds and tools into a group refreshed on demand; panels add Docker, services and logs to connected hosts.

plugins.syncHint: Secret fields are kept in the vault, which must be unlocked. A refresh keeps what you change on the hosts (favorites, keys, colors), updates name, address, user and port from the source and removes hosts that are gone.

benchmark.title: Terminal performance
benchmark.hint: Prints 8 MB of numbered lines in a new tab and times them from the first byte to the last one drawn: run it on each system and compare (target: 20 MB/s or more). "Received in" is when the last byte arrived.

benchmark.transportHint: The same 8 MB, counted but not drawn: the speed of the stream from the app to the terminal, without xterm.js.
benchmark.resultTransport: Transport only: {{mb}} MB in {{seconds}} s = {{rate}} MB/s · {{engine}} · {{os}}

usage.title: Privacy
usage.settingHint: Once a week: how often each feature was used and which well-known command-line tools (kubectl, docker, git…) ran, by name only. No identifier, host, user, path, argument or file. It helps decide what to build next.
usage.consentIntro: Shellvane can send the project anonymous usage statistics once a week. It is off unless you agree.
usage.consentWhat: What: how many times each feature was used (splits, SFTP, tunnels, environments…) and how often well-known tools like kubectl, docker or git ran, by name only; plus the app version and the system.
usage.consentNot: Never: hosts, addresses, users, paths, arguments, file names, what you type or see, or any identifier of you or this computer.
usage.consentWhere: Where: to shellvane.com, stored without your IP address, never shared or sold.
usage.consentChange: You can see exactly what is sent and change your mind in Settings › Privacy.

network.title: Network
network.intro: How Shellvane's own requests reach the internet: update checks, the gallery, the plugin store, usage reports, WebDAV and S3 sync, credential plugins; git (teams, sync) and kubectl get the same proxy. SSH connections are not affected: they use jump hosts and proxy commands.

modeHints.system: The proxy variables (HTTPS_PROXY…, also from your login shell), else the proxy set in macOS or Windows network settings. Automatic configuration (PAC) scripts are not read: use Manual then.
modeHints.manual: The proxy below, e.g. the one your company's PAC file names.

network.blocked: blocked by the company's web filter: ask IT to allow the site
